content:
I don't think both of the series are comparable... so I don't think it is really possible to choose which book is better than the other...
As you said... both of them are books of different genre... one is Fantasy the other as Romance... both of them may fall into fiction... but they are two very different books... and yes true... I do understand the boredom in Twilight books... I got really VERY bored reading New Moon...
so... to sum it all up... I think that these two series just can't be compared with each other... both are good in their own way... but yeah... I would put this much in that... maybe Twilight lacked a bit of imagination... but maybe the author never intended for it to be a fantasy... maybe Stephanie Meyer was concentrating on the romantic part more...

author: Cake
content: Meyer's vampires are sparkling fairy princesses, no joke. The only reason the Twilight books are selling so well is because Robert Pattinson and Taylor Lautner play as Edward and Jacob in the movie. Yesterday I read a chapter of each of the Twilight books (do they really deserve to be called books?), I could only read a chapter because I don't own any of Meyer's pointless love stories. So, I got onto BN.com and read an excerpt from each of them. They sucked. Seriously. Then I look at my copy of Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince and think "how I wish the rest of the series weren't packed up at the moment." I've read each of the books thirteen times (besides the last three, I've only read them four times) and I still read them over and over again. And I never get bored. I never want to put the books down. I wish there were more Harry Potter books. That's how wondrously magnificent they are. But the Twilight saga was just... horrendous.
